coaching.headline: A dominant 28-minute win: 31 kills to 11, 8 towers to 0, and 27 of the game's 33 major objectives ours, built without the support ever joining a fight.
coaching.team: Draft read four of five lanes favored, carry, midlane, offlane, and jungle, with only the support matchup against Dekker unfavored, reading "theirs all game." Khaimera opened with first blood on Bayle at 2.4, and the favored lanes held from there. Objective control stayed one-sided the rest of the way: the river ran 18 contests to 4, and the team ended up with 27 of the match's 33 major objective spawns, from the 9-minute Fangtooth through the 26-minute Primal Fangtooth. Fights snowballed on top of that. Six fights won outright between 17.8 and 26.6 fed an 8-0 tower sweep that closed the game, with zero fights lost all game. Only one of those wins, the 17.8 fight at the inner tower, wasn't converted into anything within the following 90 seconds. The one place the plan cracked: XiaO BaO's Phase was marked absent from all nine skirmishes of the game, every time out of the losing lane against Dekker. It never cost the win, since the other four lanes were carrying a bigger edge everywhere else, but that is not a plan to lean on again. Next game: get XiaO BaO's Phase out of a losing lane and into the fights she's not attending, rather than trusting the other four to keep covering for her.
coaching.whatShiftedIt: What actually broke the game open? The stretch from 20.3 to 26.6. At 20.3, Khaimera and Gideon alone caught Boris and Bayle at Fangtooth, an even 2-on-2, and won it 2-0. At 21.7 the whole group, minus the support in her losing lane, won the Orb Prime fight 4-2. Two more clean wins, 4-1 at the inhibitor at 23.7 while down a body, 3 versus 4, and 4-1 again at 26.6 while down two bodies, 3 versus 5, pushed the second inhibitor down and closed the game. Every one of those fights was won outright, with zero fights lost across the whole 28 minutes.
coaching.whatWorked: The one throughline: winning fights and immediately spending them. Five of six won fights were cashed into a tower or objective within 90 seconds, from the 20.3 Fangtooth win to the 26.6 inhibitor push. That habit, paired with 27 of the game's 33 major objectives and 78,289 damage to objectives, is why the game closed at 28 minutes with 8 towers to 0.

Six kills, two deaths, and 24,735 hero damage came on the back of a completed Solaris, Ashbringer, and Imperator core, the exact 51.9% winning core for the hero, plus an extra Tainted Rounds. The 31,616 damage to objectives was the second-highest on the team behind Khaimera's, and it shows up directly in the tower push. Both deaths, at 19.5 to Sparrow and 22.3 to The Fey, came inside team fights the squad still won.

The full Azure Core, Combustion, Wraith Leggings core came online fast, with the Wraith Leggings spike hitting at minute 12. The only death, at 11.7, landed inside an even 2-2 team fight rather than a solo mistake, and Gideon closed out The Fey again at 22.4 in the Orb Prime fight.
perPlayer.2f18e4e0-02dc-4083-a461-a4d0a52922c4: B4-Gl0Ck's Greystone had the best game on the team by the count, 10 kills, 1 death, and 39,519 hero damage, in a lane that read "ours all game" against Bayle. The build hit Sky Splitter and Aegis Of Agawar plus an off-meta Tainted Blade rather than the listed Overlord and Rapture core, and the facts flag it directly: no armor built into a comp that ran three physical damage dealers. It didn't cost the game. Greystone still took the most mitigated damage on the team, 30,686, and died only once, at 11.8 inside an even trade, but the flag is a real one for the next physical-heavy matchup.
perPlayer.cb45b649-1265-4702-974b-92800657874d: XiaO BaO's Phase never died, 0 kills and 0 deaths, and put up the team's highest healing, 17,049, and most wards, 15, in a lane that read "theirs all game" against Dekker. The cost of that losing lane showed up everywhere else: the macro marks Phase absent, out of a losing lane, from all nine skirmishes of the game, including the 21.7 Orb Prime fight and the 26.6 fight that closed the second inhibitor. The team won every one of those without her, but a support who can't reach a single fight is asking the other four to keep covering that gap.
perPlayer.a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e: Xeebs' Khaimera led the team in both damage taken, 47,963, and damage to objectives, 32,008, going 6 kills and 7 deaths in a jungle matchup that read "ours all game" against Boris. Two of those seven deaths were caught alone outside any team fight, at 7.7 to The Fey and 16.7 to Boris, a pattern worth fixing even in a blowout win. The other five deaths came inside team fights - two even trades at 14.4 and 19.1, two wins at 21.7 and 23.7 - so most of the trade was survivable here, but solo deaths early are exactly what a tougher opponent punishes.

a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.text: Xeebs' Khaimera racked up seven deaths, two of them caught alone outside any fight, next to a team-high 32,008 damage to objectives — the jungle carried tempo and gave bodies back for it.

21.7.call: Orb Prime was the largest fight of the night, won 4-2 with everyone but the support, who was still down in a losing lane. Winning it two kills clear with a body missing from the group is the standard the rest of the game should be judged against.

23.7.call: The first inhibitor fell right after the 23.7 fight, won 4-1 while down a body, 3 versus 4. Taking the structure the moment a fight like that closes, instead of resetting, is what kept the tower push moving toward the eventual 8-0 sweep.

26.6.call: The second inhibitor went down 4-1 at 26.6 even though the group was outnumbered, 3 versus 5, before the fight even started. That is the shape worth repeating: closing out a fight even while outnumbered, the way the team did here.

ccab3e43-2b89-4d42-b2cb-27129efd1b49.build: TwinBlast hit the full metaCore, Solaris, Ashbringer, and Imperator, the 51.9% winning core for the hero, then added Tainted Rounds as an off-meta fourth slot instead of a defensive item. Solaris' empowered attacks heal on hit, Ashbringer trims his cooldowns with every hit, and Imperator makes his critical strikes hit harder, a crit-scaling trio that matches his kit's own triple-shot proc. Tainted Rounds traded that fourth slot for a healing cut on-hit, a read on enemy sustain that mattered less here since the enemy team listed no healers at all. The 24,735 hero damage and 6 kills against 2 deaths say the crit package carried the lane regardless of whether the fourth item found its mark.
ccab3e43-2b89-4d42-b2cb-27129efd1b49.eternal: Demiurge suits a stat-stacking crit carry: TwinBlast's build is almost entirely raw crit chance, attack speed, and power, and Demiurge's item-stat boost multiplies every one of those numbers along with the damage his item effects deal. It adds no durability or sustain of its own, so a hyper-carry running it needs a frontline holding aggro in front of him, which held up this game since Greystone absorbed the most mitigated damage on the team.

10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.build: Willy Guggenheim's Gideon hit the complete metaCore, Azure Core, Combustion, and Wraith Leggings, the hero's 57.6% winning core, with no off-meta swaps and the fastest spike on the team, Wraith Leggings online by minute 12. Azure Core's on-cast shield and stacking mana keep him alive through poke, Combustion detonates area damage around whatever it hits, and Wraith Leggings adds bonus magic damage to every ability, stacking with Combustion's own blast radius. That fully-built core is a large part of why 36,319 hero damage arrived early enough for the midlane read to stay "ours early, even late" instead of slipping further.
10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.eternal: Vesh fits an area-burst mage: Cosmic Rift and Black Hole both hit multiple enemies at once, and Vesh's lingering damage tick on every ability hit rewards exactly that spread. The trade is no added durability, so the loadout bets on landing the combo and disengaging rather than trading blows, which matches a game where his only death came inside an even fight rather than to a solo dive.

2f18e4e0-02dc-4083-a461-a4d0a52922c4.build: B4-Gl0Ck's Greystone skipped the metaCore's Overlord and Rapture for Sky Splitter and Tainted Blade alongside the shared Aegis Of Agawar, and the facts flag it directly: no armor built into a comp that ran three physical damage dealers. Sky Splitter's current-health damage and Tainted Blade's healing cut are duelist tools, not the raw health-stacking and cleave Overlord would have added, and against an enemy team with no listed healers, the healing-cut half of that trade did little. It didn't cost the game, Greystone still absorbed the most mitigated damage on the team and died only once, but the same build against a heavier physical lineup or a real healing target would need Overlord's health back in the slot.
2f18e4e0-02dc-4083-a461-a4d0a52922c4.eternal: Krix's flat health bonus is a clean fit for an immortal frontline bruiser who wants raw survivability over burst, stacking on top of whatever health items are actually bought, Aegis Of Agawar in this build. The trade against a damage-focused loadout is straightforward: no bonus to Greystone's own poke or execute damage, purely more health to soak, which fits a kit whose win condition is fronting the fight and resetting it with the stasis ultimate rather than finishing it himself.

cb45b649-1265-4702-974b-92800657874d.build: XiaO BaO's Phase skipped the metaCore's Enra's Blessing for Hexbound Bracers and Windcaller alongside the shared Marshal and Galaxy Greaves. Enra's Blessing automatically shields a nearby ally the instant they're locked down, exactly the proactive peel tool a losing lane against Dekker's catch kit could have used; Hexbound Bracers and Windcaller instead lean into her own sustain and shared movement speed rather than a teammate's protection. The trade showed up in the macro: Phase put up the team's highest healing, 17,049, and the most wards, 15, but was marked absent from all nine skirmishes of the game, every time out of a losing lane. A shield that fires the moment an ally gets locked down is the more proactive tool for a support stuck behind and trying to force herself into fights rather than farm safety from range.
cb45b649-1265-4702-974b-92800657874d.eternal: Vesh turns Phase into more of a damage-dealing support: Energy Lance and Psychic Flare are both ability hits, and each one leaves the same scaling damage tick Vesh gives Gideon. Paired with a build that already skipped the shield item, both choices double down on the same bet, Phase hurting people rather than protecting them, so her whole protective value rests on positioning rather than any item or Eternal tool, a riskier profile for a support already stuck in a losing lane the whole game.

a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.build: Xeebs skipped the metaCore's Basilisk and Rapture for Manta Scythe and Sky Splitter alongside the shared Overlord, and the facts flag the same gap as Greystone's: no armor against a three-physical enemy comp. Overlord's permanent health-stacking passive backs a duelist who wants to outlast a fight, but Manta Scythe is built for clearing camps and minions faster rather than dueling heroes, and Sky Splitter's current-health damage carries none of the armor-shredding Basilisk or the sustained on-hit damage and lifesteal Rapture would have added. That gap shows up in the box score: Khaimera took the most damage on the team, 47,963, across seven deaths, two of them caught alone outside any clustered fight. The team still won because the other four lanes were dominant, but Basilisk's armor shred and health would have made those extended jungle duels safer.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.eternal: Demiurge multiplies whatever raw stats are already on the build, suiting a jungler leaning into item-stacking sustain rather than a cooldown-reliant kit. The trade is that durability comes entirely from the items themselves, not the Eternal, so a build already light on armor gets no cushion from the loadout to compensate, the same gap the matchup flag calls out.

threats: Chain-CC risk (1 hard-CC abilities, ~0.5s of lockdown): Bayle Kingslayer (knockback). Don't group tight into it — stagger the engage and hold mobility/cleanse for the key one.
synergy: Little hard CC on our side — we can't force a pick. Play for poke/objectives and punish their cooldowns, don't flip coin-toss 5v5s.
We have sustain (Phase) — favor the longer fight where our heals out-grind them.
Strong AoE/teamfight kit — group at choke points and fight on top of objectives.
